title: Meghaduta (Cloud-Messenger), in Translations of Shakuntala and Other Works

publication.edition: Ryder translation in Translations of Shakuntala and Other Works; some library catalogues date the same translation 1914; Sanskrit original c. 4th-5th century CE; poem runs about 111-119 verses depending on recension (commonly cited as 111)

verification.verification_notes: Bibliographic identity (Ryder translation, Dent Everyman's 1912, with 1914 appearing in some library catalogues; Project Gutenberg #16659) and structural facts (an exiled yaksha asks a passing cloud to carry his message to his beloved; verse count varies by recension, approximately 110-121, commonly 111) confirmed via library catalogues, Project Gutenberg, and reference records on web search 2026-09-24. Described only; no verse text reproduced.

limitations: Verse count and lineation vary across recensions and English translations; no single rendering's stanza numbering is relied on.

copyright.notes: Sanskrit original ancient; 1912 Dent/Ryder translation public domain; analytical citation only, no verse text reproduced.
